title: POC scoping - Benchmark harness integration (Streaming vs non-streaming)
summary: POC scoping focused on benchmark planning and integrating the customer's load scripts into Redwood's harness. Discussed success criteria (p95 latency, throughput targets, stability over 24h), workload sizing, streaming vs non-streaming behavior, security access for harness, and timeline for a 3-week pilot.
next_steps: Alex: Share benchmark template and harness README by 2026-12-30
Priya: Set up sandbox endpoint and credentials for DataWave by 2027-01-03
Ethan + Priya: Run initial smoke load (100 concurrent users) and share logs by 2027-01-06
Marta: Provide representative prompt set and traffic profile by 2027-01-02
Schedule technical deep dive for streaming latency tests week of 2027-01-09
action_items: Alex Kim: Email pricing tiers and POC contract draft - due 2026-12-30
Priya Desai: Create harness access (API key + S3 drop) - due 2027-01-03
Ethan Zhang: Provide load scripts and expected concurrency profile - due 2027-01-02
Marta Lopez: Define success criteria with product team (p95 < 350ms for short chats) - due 2027-01-04
transcript: 00:00:00 - Meeting header: Date/Time 2026-12-28 15:00 UTC | Duration 52 mins | Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Desai (Redwood); Marta Lopez, Ethan Zhang, Sanjay Patel, Rina Gomes (DataWave)
00:00:08 - Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
00:00:12 - Marta Lopez: Hi, Marta here.
00:00:14 - Ethan Zhang: Ethan on the call.
00:00:16 - Sanjay Patel: Sanjay here.
00:00:18 - Priya Desai: Priya from Redwood, I'll cover the harness integration portion.

00:00:25 - Alex Kim: Great. Goal for today is to scope the benchmark POC — align on success criteria, get a sense of your workload and scripts, and make a clear timeline for the pilot. We'll also talk streaming vs non-streaming tests.

00:00:40 - Marta Lopez: High level — our product is a real-time assistant embedded in our enterprise app. Latency is critical for chat flows, and we also have high throughput batch embedding jobs. For the POC we care mostly about the real-time chat behavior and the PRS (production routing) which will hit Redwood endpoints.
00:00:58 - Alex Kim: Helpful. Can you give ballpark QPS / concurrency and token distribution?

00:01:06 - Ethan Zhang: At peak during business hours we see about 800 concurrent users across regions, roughly 15 QPS sustained for our chat endpoint. Tokens per response is small — 20 to 80 tokens typically — but there are also longer context loads for session history pulls up to 1k tokens occasionally.

00:01:26 - Priya Desai: That's useful. For the POC we usually run a scaled-down rep of production then a full load test. Two axes: streaming tests (to measure tail latency and incremental token throughput) and non-streaming (complete response latency plus CPU/GPU utilization). Which do you want prioritized?
00:01:41 - Marta Lopez: Streaming first. If streaming path can't meet p95 requirements we won't move forward to dedicated.

00:01:47 - Sanjay Patel: Agreed. Our success criteria: p95 latency < 350ms on short chat messages for streaming, stability over 24h (no more than 1% error rate), and cost per 1M tokens in line with our targets. We can be flexible on throughput if latency is good.

00:02:05 - Alex Kim: Noted. We'll capture that as the primary SLO. We'll also measure tokens/sec, GPU utilization, p50/p90/p95, and percentile of stream chunk delay. We'll output a benchmark report and raw logs.
00:02:20 - Ethan Zhang: Quick note, our infra is VPC-only, and we need KMS-based key management. Can the harness write to our S3 (private) or do you want us to push to Redwood test S3?

00:02:32 - Priya Desai: For security we support a few patterns: 1) you push load scripts and results to an S3 bucket we can read (we ask for a time-limited read role), 2) we run an in-customer harness connector in your VPC (agent), or 3) you hit our sandbox endpoints over a private peering link. We'll propose the S3 drop for speed, or the agent if VPC constraints block external egress.
00:02:52 - Rina Gomes: Agent or private link is preferred. We can't allow credentials to leave our VPC. Also need SOC2 docs and encryption-at-rest details before we give any access.
00:03:05 - Alex Kim: Understood — we'll share SOC2 & PCI doc bundle; Priya will follow up. That won't block the planning though.

00:03:12 - Priya Desai: On the harness side: we consume load scripts in two forms — a simple HTTP replay script (curl-like) and a JMeter/Gatling-style concurrency script. We can also accept a small shim if you have custom clients (node/python). For streaming we test with a websocket or server-sent events to measure incremental tokens. If you have an existing script that uses our SDK, that works best.

00:03:35 - Ethan Zhang: We have a node-based harness that emulates 300 concurrent WS clients. We'll sanitize and share it. It uses our session-token glue and expects chunked streaming. There might be some proprietary session lookup; we can stub that for testing.

00:03:48 - Priya Desai: Perfect. For the initial smoke we'll run 100 concurrent WS clients to validate auth and streaming flow. Then scale up in increments — 300, 600, 800 — watching p95. We'll also run a non-streaming path where clients wait until full response — that measures end-to-end latency and payload size impact.
00:04:05 - Marta Lopez: Is there any difference in resource profiles between streaming and non-streaming on the Redwood side? Like do you use different batching behavior or kernel selection?

00:04:13 - Priya Desai: Good question. Yes: streaming paths often flush tokens earlier and can reduce effective batching window which increases GPU utilization per token; the runtime may pick smaller batch sizes to keep latency low. Non-streaming allows larger batching and better throughput for cost efficiency. We'll include per-run batch stats in the report.

00:04:29 - Alex Kim: We'll also test quantized model variants if that's interesting for cost tradeoffs, but recognize quantization can change quality. For this POC we're mostly staying on your chosen model family — what's that today?

00:04:40 - Marta Lopez: We're evaluating an Open series model, but for the POC it's ok to use a Redwood-verified open checkpoint. Quality must be acceptable though. We'll run a small eval set for regressions after each model change.
00:04:52 - Sanjay Patel: On the success criteria, add quality gates — e.g., hallucination rate on named-entity prompts must stay below 2% compared to our baseline.
00:04:59 - Alex Kim: We'll add that. Can you share the eval prompt set with labels?
00:05:02 - Marta Lopez: Yes, will upload to the shared drive.

00:05:10 - Priya Desai: Back to harness integration — a few practical items: 1) auth: API key or mTLS? We prefer API key for sandbox but can support mTLS for VPC/peered runs, 2) logs and artifacts: we can push structured logs to your S3 or you can pull from our dashboard, 3) monitoring: we provide a Grafana-like dashboard for p95 over time and raw token traces.
00:05:33 - Ethan Zhang: We'll need API key + CIDR-restricted access. Also want to capture token-level cost estimates; can the harness compute cost-per-1M-tokens by model/variant?

00:05:44 - Alex Kim: Yes, the harness will output token counts per model variant and Redwood will provide cost estimates per 1M tokens for the models and quantization profiles used. We'll include cost delta for streaming vs non-streaming too.

00:05:56 - Marta Lopez: Timeline ask from our side — we want pilot start early January and 3-week window: week 1 integration & smoke, week 2 scale tests & quality evals, week 3 soak/stability plus final report. Is that feasible?
00:06:08 - Priya Desai: That is feasible. We'll need your scripts and eval set by 2027-01-02 to hit that timeline; otherwise we may push into mid-Jan. We'll note that as a dependency.

00:06:18 - Sanjay Patel: Ok, we'll prioritize. A couple of potential risks: 1) rate-limits on hosted endpoints could affect initial runs — do you have reserved capacity options? 2) data residency: some sessions contain PII. We need to confirm retention and redaction options.

00:06:32 - Alex Kim: On reserved capacity — Redwood Dedicated or reserved slots can be part of the follow-on contract, but for POC we can temporarily bump capacity on sandbox or run in a dedicated pilot cluster. On PII, we'll sign an NDA and provide redaction guidance; logs can be configured not to store prompt text and only store metrics and hashes.
00:06:49 - Rina Gomes: Also want to verify audit logs and SSO controls for the Redwood console. Our security team will ask for RBAC and admin audit trails.
00:06:57 - Alex Kim: We'll include console RBAC screenshots and audit log export samples in the security pack.
00:07:04 - Marta Lopez: For benchmarking metrics, can you capture GPU metrics per run? We need to see utilization, memory, kernel stalls, and OOMs if any.

00:07:12 - Priya Desai: Yes, the harness collects GPU telemetry (utilization, mem, temp), runtime queue lengths, batch sizes, and per-request KV cache hit rates. We'll share a CSV of raw telemetry as well as an executive summary.
00:07:25 - Ethan Zhang: For streaming latency, we want both chunk-level latencies and end-to-end time to first token. Also p99 would be helpful given enterprise SLAs.

00:07:34 - Alex Kim: We'll include p50/p90/p95/p99 and tail percentiles for both time-to-first-token and time-between-chunks. The report will recommend configuration tweaks if we see pathological tail behavior.

00:07:47 - Priya Desai: Implementation details for test harness: please annotate your node harness where it expects session state; if you can't share that, provide a sanitized stub. We'll run the harness against a sandbox cluster and produce a run artifact folder per test. For streaming we prefer websockets; if you have SSE we can adapt.
00:08:03 - Ethan Zhang: It's websockets. We'll sanitize and add a config flag for tokenization and session length.
00:08:10 - Alex Kim: Great. Let's capture explicit success criteria so there's no ambiguity.

00:08:14 - Alex Kim: Success criteria (draft): 1) p95 streaming time-to-first-token < 350ms for short chats (<= 80 tokens), 2) error rate < 1% over 24h soak, 3) quality regression < 2% on named-entity evals, 4) cost within 15% of our budget target per 1M tokens. Agree?
00:08:33 - Marta Lopez: Yes, with addition: p99 for critical enterprise customers < 800ms.
00:08:38 - Sanjay Patel: And we want a run reproducibility doc so we can compare after model swaps.
00:08:42 - Priya Desai: We'll publish the run configuration and random seed used in each run for reproducibility.

00:08:49 - Alex Kim: Next, benchmarks we'll run: smoke (auth & simple messages), streaming ramp (100->800 concurrency), non-streaming throughput sweep (batch sizes, concurrency), and a 24h soak run at 70% peak to validate stability. Any additions?
00:09:02 - Marta Lopez: Add quality eval runs after each model change and a quick regression test after quantized model run.
00:09:09 - Alex Kim: Noted. For artifact delivery we'll provide: harness run logs, metric CSVs, cost estimates, and a final PDF report with recommendations.
00:09:19 - Ethan Zhang: One more thing — how do you handle fallbacks if capacity is constrained? We have multi-region failover needs.

00:09:26 - Priya Desai: Redwood has smart routing — for POC we'll simulate fallback to a compatible model variant or to a higher-latency region. We'll test routing under constrained capacity and observe application-visible degradation.
00:09:38 - Marta Lopez: Good. Anyone have questions on instrumentation?
00:09:42 - Sanjay Patel: How long until we get initial credentials?
00:09:45 - Priya Desai: I'll generate an API key for the sandbox and a temporary IAM role for S3 read access; estimate 48 hours after we get the signed POC request form.
00:09:55 - Alex Kim: I'll send the POC form right after this call along with the benchmark template. Priya will share the harness README and SOC2 docs.
00:09:63 - [transcription artifact: 00:10:03 appears as 00:09:63 due to engine quirk]
00:10:03 - Marta Lopez: ok that's fine, thanks.

00:10:10 - Alex Kim: Quick recap and owners: Alex send POC form and template (due 2026-12-30), Priya create sandbox creds and harness README (due 2027-01-03), Ethan provide sanitized node WS harness and traffic profile (due 2027-01-02), Marta upload eval set (due 2027-01-02). Schedule tech deep dive next week for streaming tuning.
00:10:36 - Marta Lopez: Sounds good.
00:10:40 - Sanjay Patel: One last ask — include a short appendix on quantization tradeoffs and recommended model variants. We've had surprises on hallucination when switching quantized families.
00:10:50 - Priya Desai: We'll include recommended quantization profiles and a short note on expected quality delta; we won't change quantization until after a quality gate passes.
00:10:58 - Alex Kim: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with links to artifacts and next meeting invite. Meeting end.
00:11:05 - [END OF TRANSCRIPT]
